messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis

Details:
The test failure and the bug report indicate that the method `ClassUtils.getShortClassName(Class<?>)` behaves incorrectly for array classes by appending a semicolon at the end of the returned short class name.

Looking at the snippet of `ClassUtils.getShortClassName(Class<?>)` (lines 168-173), this method:
- Checks if the input class is null.
- If not null, calls `getShortClassName` with the result of `cls.getName()` (the class's full name as a String).

The method `ClassUtils.getShortClassName(String)` (lines 183-204) then processes the string class name:
- It returns empty string for null or empty input.
- The comment "Handle array encoding" at line 192 suggests intended handling of array class names.
- However, there is no actual code shown that extracts or removes the array notation or the leading character(s) used in Java array type names (e.g., '[Ljava.lang.String;').
- The method simply locates the last package separator '.' and extracts the substring after it (line 199).
- Also, it replaces inner class separator '$' with '.' (lines 200-201).
- It then returns the extracted substring (line 203).

This logic does not handle the array class name format correctly:
- Array classes in Java have names like "[Ljava.lang.String;".
- The `getName()` of an array class includes brackets and semicolon.
- Simply taking substring after last '.' will result in "String;" (with the unwanted semicolon).
- This explains why the test expects "String[]" but gets "String;" instead.

The current bug report explicitly states that a semicolon is appended to the end of array class names.

Hence, the root cause of the bug is the incomplete or missing handling of array class names in `ClassUtils.getShortClassName(String)` to properly convert the internal array encodings (e.g., '[L', trailing ';', etc.) to a readable array notation (like "String[]").

The test `test_getShortClassName_Class()` expects this correct array notation but fails because the code currently returns the internal representation substring with semicolon instead.

No recent bug reports are relevant to this array name handling issue.

Summary:
- `getShortClassName(Class<?>)` calls `getShortClassName(String)` with class's `getName()`.
- `getShortClassName(String)` lacks correct logic to parse and convert array class name encoding.
- This causes semicolon to remain in output for array classes.
- Leading to test failure as described in the current bug report.

Fixing should add proper detection and conversion logic for array class names in `ClassUtils.getShortClassName(String)`.

The faulty or missing logic is indicated by the comment "// Handle array encoding" without any implementation.

This is the cause of the bug and test failure.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
